rationale: RUST-MR re-measured (2026-10-03). `declaration-position-reads` already pins the BARE `extern "C"` fn-pointer shape; what it did not cover is the shape the dropped `parenthesized_type` literal was written for, and that is the whole justification for dropping it. Every fn-pointer spelling below must reach the ONE live guard arm (`holder.type === "function_type"`), because the pinned tree-sitter-rust 0.24.0 grammar has neither `bare_function_type` (0 occurrences over 359 corpus files) nor `parenthesized_type` (0 occurrences), and the parentheses of `(fn(a: u32))` parse as a `tuple_type` around a `function_type` — measured on the pinned wasm by script/m14/rust-fnptr-grammar-probe.ts. Those two names were the analyzer's only UNKNOWN node-type literals (`audit-analyzer-grammar --lang rust`: refs=86 unknown=2; `verify-fixture-coverage`: deadLiterals=2) and were branches no input could reach. THE FIXTURE IS LOAD-BEARING BY CONSTRUCTION: each parameter name is `use`-imported, and a declaration-position name only publishes a read when it also RESOLVES, so with the guard deleted this file emits 4 extra `uses` edges (`global -> schema` @43, `global -> cb` @43, `global -> paren_schema` @46, `global -> name` @52) and every forbid row below flips. The positive control keeps the guard from passing by over-reaching.

expectRelationships.comment: THE CONTROL. A real function's parameter is excluded by the per-function bound-name set, not by this guard, so the same imported leaf read from a real function still publishes. Without this row the guard could be suppressing reads wholesale and the fixture would stay green.
